docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The API layer acts as the interface between external clients and the ML platform. It exposes endpoints for:

  • Model inference
  • Data ingestion triggers
  • Model management
  • Health and monitoring

The API is designed using FastAPI for high performance, async support, and automatic documentation.

docs.text:
• Stateless services
  • RESTful design
  • Async-first (non-blocking I/O)
  • Separation of concerns
  • Scalable and containerized
  • Secure by default

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text: This document outlines the key assumptions made during the design and implementation of the MLOps pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Data Assumptions
docs.text:
• Data sources (e.g., APIs, web scraping) are available and stable.
  • Incoming data follows a semi-structured or structured format.
  • Data schema changes are infrequent and manageable.
  • Missing values and anomalies are within acceptable limits.

docs.title: 2. Infrastructure Assumptions
docs.text:
• Cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) services are reliable and highly available.
  • Required services (S3, EC2, ECR, Kubernetes, etc.) are provisioned correctly.
  • Network latency is within acceptable bounds for real-time inference (if applicable).

docs.title: 3. Model Assumptions
docs.text:
• Historical data is representative of future data (stationarity assumption).
  • Model performance degradation is gradual (not abrupt).
  • Training data is sufficiently labeled and clean.

docs.title: 4. Deployment Assumptions
docs.text:
• CI/CD pipelines execute successfully without frequent failures.
  • Docker images are compatible across environments.
  • Kubernetes cluster has sufficient resources for scaling.

docs.title: 5. Security Assumptions
docs.text:
• IAM roles and permissions are correctly configured.
  • Secrets are securely stored (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Vault).
  • No unauthorized access to data or services.

docs.title: 6. Monitoring Assumptions
docs.text:
• Logging and monitoring systems (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki) are operational.
  • Alerts are configured correctly and reach the responsible team.

docs.title: 7. Team & Process Assumptions
docs.text:
• Developers follow coding standards and contribution guidelines.
  • Version control practices (Git branching, PR reviews) are enforced.
  • Documentation is kept up to date.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: These assumptions define the expected operating conditions of the system. Any deviation from these assumptions may impact system performance, reliability, or scalability.

docs.title: Future Work
docs.text: This document outlines potential enhancements and future directions for the MLOps system.

docs.title: 1. Data Pipeline Enhancements
docs.text:
• Implement real-time data ingestion using Kafka or streaming frameworks.

docs.title: 2. Model Improvements
docs.text:

  • Implement online learning / continuous training.
  • Add automated model selection and hyperparameter tuning.

docs.title: 3. Deployment Enhancements

docs.title: 4. Observability Improvements
docs.text:

  • Unified dashboard for ML + business KPIs.

docs.title: 5. CI/CD Improvements

docs.title: 8. Advanced MLOps Capabilities

docs.title: 9. Developer Experience

docs.title: Summary

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: This document outlines the known limitations of the current MLOps system.

docs.title: 1. Data Limitations
docs.text:
• Data quality depends on external sources (e.g., web scraping reliability).
  • Limited handling of schema drift.
  • No real-time streaming ingestion (batch-focused pipeline).

docs.title: 2. Model Limitations
docs.text:
• Model retraining is scheduled or triggered, not fully autonomous.
  • Limited support for advanced model architectures (e.g., large-scale transformers).
  • No online learning or continuous training capability.

docs.title: 3. Infrastructure Limitations
docs.text:
• Scaling depends on pre-configured Kubernetes autoscaling policies.
  • Infrastructure provisioning via Terraform may require manual intervention in edge cases.
  • Multi-region deployment is not fully implemented.

docs.title: 4. Monitoring & Observability Limitations
docs.text:
• Limited support for advanced anomaly detection in logs/metrics.
  • Alerting may generate false positives if thresholds are not tuned.
  • No unified dashboard for business + ML metrics.

docs.title: 5. CI/CD Limitations
docs.text:
• Pipeline execution time may increase with scale.
  • Limited rollback automation in complex failure scenarios.
  • Dependency on third-party tools (GitHub Actions, Jenkins).

docs.title: 6. Security Limitations
docs.text:
• No zero-trust architecture implemented.
  • Limited automated security audits.
  • Manual review required for IAM policy changes.

docs.title: 7. Cost Limitations
docs.text:
• Costs may increase significantly with scaling.
  • No fully automated cost optimization system.
  • Resource over-provisioning may occur during peak loads.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: While the system is production-ready, these limitations highlight areas where improvements can enhance robustness, scalability, and efficiency.

docs.text:

  • Use meaningful variable and function names

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
def calculate_accuracy(y_true: list, y_pred: list) -> float:
    """
    Calculate accuracy between true and predicted labels.
    """
    correct = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == p)
    return correct / len(y_true)
````

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Least privilege ensures that identities only have permissions necessary to perform their tasks.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Start with zero permissions
  • Add permissions incrementally
  • Use resource-level restrictions
  • Apply condition-based access

docs.title: Example Policy (S3 Restricted Access)
docs.text:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::ml-platform-dev-data/*"
    }
  ]
}
````

### 1. Resource-Level Permissions

* S3 buckets

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This project follows a multi-layered testing strategy to ensure reliability, scalability, and correctness across:

  • Infrastructure (Terraform)
  • Application Code (API, ML logic)
  • ML Pipeline (data → training → inference)
  • End-to-End System

docs.title: Testing Pyramid
docs.text:
We follow a modified testing pyramid:

        ┌──────────────┐
        │   E2E Tests  │
        ├──────────────┤
        │ Integration  │
        ├──────────────┤
        │   Unit Tests │
        └──────────────┘
     + Terraform & Synthetic Tests

docs.title: Test Categories
docs.text: Type Purpose Terraform Tests Validate infra correctness Unit Tests Validate individual functions/modules Integration Tests Validate service interactions E2E Tests Validate full system workflow Synthetic Tests Monitor production health

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Test early (shift-left testing)
  • Automate everything in CI/CD
  • Keep tests isolated and reproducible
  • Use mocks for external dependencies
  • Ensure idempotency (especially for infra)

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
All tests are executed in pipeline:

  1. Terraform validation → terraform validate
  2. Terraform tests → tftest
  3. Unit tests → pytest
  4. Integration tests → staged environment
  5. E2E tests → deployed system
  6. Synthetic tests → post-deployment monitoring

## Mocking

Use mocks for:

* External APIs
* Databases
* S3 interactions

Example:

```python
from unittest.mock import patch

@patch("boto3.client")
def test_s3_upload(mock_s3):
    upload_file()
    mock_s3.assert_called_once()
